commands.name: azure-gpu
commands.description: Request, use and release Azure GPU VMs (A100/H100/T4) for training, RL fine-tuning, vLLM serving or paper-replication jobs. Use whenever a task needs a GPU and none is attached to this machine. Wraps `az` with size allowlist, TTL tags, auto-shutdown and a reaper so nothing is left running. (user)

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: schedule
commands.description: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: workflow-authoring
commands.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

commands.name: run-skill-generator
commands.description: Author or improve the run-<unit> skill - a per-project skill that tells agents how to build, launch, and drive this project's app. Use when the user asks to set up the project, get it running, write run instructions, or verify build/run steps work from a clean environment.

commands.description: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: docx
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: google-workspace
commands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: import-memory
commands.description: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: morning
commands.description: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pdf
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pptx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: skill-creator
commands.description: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: xlsx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved. (claude.ai sync)

"""Build the text corpora used throughout the project.

  text, ai (1 = machine-written), dataset, group (pair id), domain, generator, split
plus data/processed/steer_prompts.jsonl (held-out HC3 questions for generation).

import ast, json, os, random, re
import pandas as pd

random.seed(0)
OUT = "data/processed"
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)


def detok(s: str) -> str:
    """Undo the PTB-style tokenisation in HC3 (applied to both sides, so it cannot
    act as an authorship cue)."""
    s = s.replace(" ", " ")
    s = re.sub(r" ([.,!?;:%)\]}])", r"\1", s)
    s = re.sub(r"([(\[{$]) ", r"\1", s)
    s = re.sub(r" (n't|'s|'re|'ve|'ll|'d|'m)\b", r"\1", s)
    s = re.sub(r" ' (s|re|ve|ll|d|m|t)\b", r"'\1", s)
    s = re.sub(r'" ([^"]*?) "', r'"\1"', s)
    s = re.sub(r" - ", "-", s) if re.search(r"\w - \w", s) and s.count(" - ") > 3 else s
    s = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip()
    return s


def as_list(x):
    if isinstance(x, list):
        return x
    try:
        return ast.literal_eval(x)
    except Exception:
        return [x]


def write(name, rows):
    with open(f"{OUT}/{name}.jsonl", "w") as f:
        for r in rows:
            f.write(json.dumps(r) + "\n")
    print(name, len(rows))


# ---------------- HC3: question-matched human vs ChatGPT answers -------------
caps = {"reddit_eli5": 900, "finance": 600, "medicine": 600, "open_qa": 600, "wiki_csai": 600}
hc3 = [json.loads(l) for l in open("data/HC3/all.jsonl")]
random.shuffle(hc3)
by_dom = {}
for ex in hc3:
    h, c = as_list(ex["human_answers"]), as_list(ex["chatgpt_answers"])
    if not h or not c:
        continue
    h, c = detok(h[0]), detok(c[0])
    if len(h.split()) < 30 or len(c.split()) < 30:
        continue
    by_dom.setdefault(ex["source"], []).append((detok(ex["question"]), h, c))
rows, prompts = [], []
for dom, items in by_dom.items():

    for i, (q, h, c) in enumerate(items[: caps[dom] + n_steer]):

write("steer_prompts", prompts)

        "llama-3-70B-Instruct": "llama3-70b-inst", "llama-3-8B-Instruct": "llama3-8b-inst",
        "llama-3-70B": "llama3-70b-base", "llama-3-8B": "llama3-8b-base"}
P = "data/human-ai-parallel-corpus/text_data/hape-text_{}.parquet"
hum = pd.read_parquet(P.format("human-chunk-2"))
hum["doc"] = hum.doc_id.str.split("@").str[0]
docs = sorted(hum.doc.unique())
random.shuffle(docs)
docs = docs[:1800]
split_of = {d: ("train" if random.random() < 0.7 else "test") for d in docs}
hum = hum.set_index("doc")
rows = []
for d in docs:
    rows.append(dict(text=hum.loc[d, "text"], ai=0, dataset="hap", group=d, domain=d.split("_")[0],
                     generator="human", split=split_of[d]))
for f, g in gens.items():
    df = pd.read_parquet(P.format(f))
    df["doc"] = df.doc_id.str.split("@").str[0]
    df = df.set_index("doc")
    for d in docs:
        if d in df.index:
            rows.append(dict(text=df.loc[d, "text"], ai=1, dataset="hap", group=d, domain=d.split("_")[0],
                             generator=g, split=split_of[d]))
write("hap", rows)

# ---------------- MAGE: out-of-distribution, many generators -----------------
m = pd.read_csv("data/MAGE/test.csv").dropna()
m["ai"] = 1 - m.label
m["domain"] = m.src.str.split("_").str[0]
m["generator"] = m.src.apply(lambda s: "human" if s.endswith("human") else s.split("_machine_")[-1])
chat = m[m.generator.str.contains("gpt-3.5|davinci-003")]
old = m[(m.ai == 1) & ~m.generator.str.contains("gpt-3.5|davinci")]
hm = m[m.ai == 0]
sel = pd.concat([hm.sample(1200, random_state=0), chat.sample(600, random_state=0), old.sample(600, random_state=0)])
rows = [dict(text=r.text, ai=int(r.ai), dataset="mage", group=f"mage_{i}", domain=r.domain,
             generator=r.generator, split="test") for i, r in enumerate(sel.itertuples())]
write("mage", rows)
g4 = pd.read_csv("data/MAGE/test_ood_set_gpt.csv").dropna()
rows = [dict(text=r.text, ai=int(1 - r.label), dataset="mage_gpt4", group=f"g4_{i}", domain=r.src.split("_")[0],
             generator="gpt4" if r.label == 0 else "human", split="test") for i, r in enumerate(g4.itertuples())]
write("mage_gpt4", rows)

import json, os
import numpy as np
import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
os.environ.setdefault("HF_HOME", os.path.join(ROOT, "hf_cache"))
MODELS = {"instruct": "Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct", "base": "Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B"}
MAX_TOK = 128   # every text is truncated to at most this many tokens
SKIP = 1        # first position (attention sink, huge norm) excluded from pooling


def load_jsonl(p):
    return [json.loads(l) for l in open(p)]


def load_model(which="instruct", device="cuda"):
    name = MODELS[which]
    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(name)
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(name, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map=device)
    model.eval()
    return tok, model


def token_budget(tok, rows):
    """Length control: all members of a group (same question / same prefix) are cut to
    the same number of tokens, the minimum over the group (capped at MAX_TOK)."""
    ids = [tok(r["text"], add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"] for r in rows]
    by_group = {}
    for r, i in zip(rows, ids):
        by_group[r["group"]] = min(by_group.get(r["group"], MAX_TOK), len(i))
    return [i[: by_group[r["group"]]] for r, i in zip(rows, ids)]


@torch.no_grad()
def extract(tok, model, rows, bs=16, paired=True):
    """Mean-pooled residual stream at every layer + mean token NLL.
    Returns acts [N, L+1, d] float16, nll [N], ntok [N]."""

"""Content-matched control corpora made by rewriting human text with an external LLM.

For each human source passage we ask gpt-4.1-mini (via OpenRouter) for
  formal   - very formal register
  informal - very casual register
  neutral  - a plain paraphrase (content fixed, author becomes an LLM)
formal-vs-informal gives a FORMALITY direction with authorship held fixed (both AI);
human-vs-neutral gives an AUTHORSHIP contrast with content held fixed.
"""
import json, random
from common import load_jsonl, ROOT
from llm_api import chat_many

random.seed(1)
MODEL = "openai/gpt-4.1-mini"
hap = [r for r in load_jsonl(f"{ROOT}/data/processed/hap.jsonl") if r["ai"] == 0 and r["split"] == "train"]
hc3 = [r for r in load_jsonl(f"{ROOT}/data/processed/hc3.jsonl") if r["ai"] == 0 and r["split"] == "train"]
src = random.sample(hap, 250) + random.sample(hc3, 150)
INSTR = {
    "formal": "Rewrite the following passage in a highly formal, academic register. Keep the same content and roughly the same length.",
    "informal": "Rewrite the following passage in a very casual, informal, conversational register (as if texting a friend). Keep the same content and roughly the same length.",
    "neutral": "Paraphrase the following passage. Keep the same content, meaning and roughly the same length.",
}
rows = []
for style, ins in INSTR.items():
    msgs = [[{"role": "user", "content": f"{ins} Output only the rewritten passage, nothing else.\n\nPassage:\n{' '.join(r['text'].split()[:220])}"}] for r in src]
    outs = chat_many(MODEL, msgs, temperature=0.7, max_tokens=500)
    for i, (r, o) in enumerate(zip(src, outs)):
        if o:
            rows.append(dict(text=o.strip(), style=style, group=f"rw_{i}", source_dataset=r["dataset"],
                             domain=r["domain"], ai=1))
for i, r in enumerate(src):
    rows.append(dict(text=" ".join(r["text"].split()[:220]), style="human", group=f"rw_{i}",
                     source_dataset=r["dataset"], domain=r["domain"], ai=0))
with open(f"{ROOT}/data/processed/rewrites.jsonl", "w") as f:
    for r in rows:
        f.write(json.dumps(r) + "\n")
print(len(rows))

"""Assistant-axis control (after Lu et al., 2026, simplified).

The instruct model answers a set of questions (a) as its default Assistant and
(b) while role-playing 24 non-assistant characters. We record the residual stream
mean-pooled over the RESPONSE tokens (inside the chat template) at every layer.
Assistant axis = mean(default) - mean(role-play), per layer.
We also save the generated texts so they can be read as raw text later.
usage: python assistant_axis.py {instruct|base}
For the base model we reuse the instruct model's texts (teacher-forced), so the
base-model axis is measured on identical tokens.
"""
import json, os, sys
import numpy as np
import torch
from common import load_model, ROOT, load_jsonl

which = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "instruct"
PERSONAS = ["a pirate captain from the 1700s", "a medieval peasant farmer", "a grumpy old fisherman",
            "a teenage skateboarder", "a Shakespearean actor who always speaks in verse", "a hard-boiled 1940s detective",
            "a cowboy on the American frontier", "a wise forest spirit", "a Viking warrior",
            "a sarcastic stand-up comedian", "a nervous first-year medical student", "a Victorian aristocrat",
            "a surfer dude from California", "an ancient Roman senator", "a conspiracy theorist who distrusts everything",
            "a kindergarten teacher talking to children", "a gruff army drill sergeant", "a dreamy romantic poet",
            "a street vendor in Mumbai", "a tired night-shift nurse", "a hip-hop artist",
            "a fantasy wizard", "a dog who can talk", "a ghost haunting an old house"]
QUESTIONS = ["What do you think about the weather today?", "How should I spend my weekend?",
             "What is the best way to cook an egg?", "Why do people like music?",
             "Can you tell me about yourself?", "What advice would you give a young person?",
             "How do you deal with stress?", "What makes a good friend?",
             "Why is the sky blue?", "What is your favorite food and why?",
             "How do I fix a flat bicycle tyre?", "Is money important for happiness?",
             "What do you do when you can't sleep?", "Explain how a bank loan works.",
             "What's the meaning of life?", "How should I prepare for a job interview?"]
TXT = f"{ROOT}/data/processed/assistant_axis_texts.jsonl"
tok, model = load_model("instruct" if which == "instruct" else "base")
L = model.config.num_hidden_layers + 1

if which == "instruct" and not os.path.exists(TXT):
    itok = tok
    recs = []
    conds = [("default", None)] + [(p, p) for p in PERSONAS]
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    for cname, p in conds:
        msgs_list = []
        for q in QUESTIONS:
            m = [] if p is None else [{"role": "system", "content": f"You are {p}. Stay fully in character at all times; never mention being an AI or an assistant."}]
            m.append({"role": "user", "content": q})
            msgs_list.append(m)
        prompts = [itok.apply_chat_template(m, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True) for m in msgs_list]
        itok.padding_side = "left"
        enc = itok(prompts, return_tensors="pt", padding=True).to("cuda")
        with torch.no_grad():
            out = model.generate(**enc, max_new_tokens=160, do_sample=True, temperature=0.7, top_p=0.9,
                                 pad_token_id=itok.eos_token_id)
        for q, m, o in zip(QUESTIONS, msgs_list, out[:, enc.input_ids.shape[1]:]):
            recs.append(dict(cond=cname, question=q, messages=m, response=itok.decode(o, skip_special_tokens=True).strip()))
    with open(TXT, "w") as f:
        for r in recs:
            f.write(json.dumps(r) + "\n")

recs = load_jsonl(TXT)
itok = load_model.__globals__["AutoTokenizer"].from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct")
acts = np.zeros((len(recs), L, model.config.hidden_size), dtype=np.float32)
for i, r in enumerate(recs):
    prompt = itok.apply_chat_template(r["messages"], tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True)
    p_ids = itok(prompt, add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"]
    r_ids = itok(r["response"], add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"][:160]
    ids = torch.tensor([p_ids + r_ids]).cuda()
    with torch.no_grad():
        hs = model(input_ids=ids, output_hidden_states=True).hidden_states
    acts[i] = torch.stack([h[0, len(p_ids):].float().mean(0) for h in hs]).cpu().numpy()
cond = np.array([r["cond"] for r in recs])
np.savez(f"{ROOT}/data/acts/{which}_assistant_axis.npz", acts=acts.astype(np.float16), cond=cond)
axis = acts[cond == "default"].mean(0) - acts[cond != "default"].mean(0)
np.save(f"{ROOT}/data/acts/{which}_assistant_axis_dir.npy", axis)
print("saved", axis.shape)

"""Fit all directions (per layer) from cached activations and save them.

AI directions (diff-of-means, AI minus human, fit on TRAIN splits only):
  ai_hc3   : HC3 ChatGPT answers vs human answers to the same question
  ai_hap   : HAP instruct-model continuations (gpt-4o, gpt-4o-mini, llama-3 8B/70B-Instruct) vs human continuation of the same prefix
  ai       : unit(unit(ai_hc3) + unit(ai_hap))  <- main "AI-ness" direction
Confound directions (authorship held fixed within each contrast):
  formality : Llama-3.1-8B formal rewrite - informal rewrite of the same passage (both AI)
  register  : HAP human text, acad+news - spok+tvm+fic (both human)
  domain    : HC3 human answers, encyclopedic domains - reddit_eli5 (both human)
  fluency   : human texts, lowest-NLL tertile - highest-NLL tertile (both human)
  verbosity : HC3 human answers, longest tertile (full answer) - shortest tertile
  assistant : Assistant axis = default-Assistant responses - role-play responses (Lu et al. style)
usage: python directions.py {instruct|base}
"""
import sys, json
import numpy as np
from common import load_jsonl, ROOT

INST_GENS = {"gpt-4o", "gpt-4o-mini", "llama3-70b-inst", "llama3-8b-inst"}


def load(which, ds):
    z = np.load(f"{ROOT}/data/acts/{which}_{ds}.npz")
    rows = load_jsonl(f"{ROOT}/data/processed/{ds}.jsonl")
    return rows, z["acts"], z["nll"], z["ntok"]


def dmean(A, pos, neg):
    return A[pos].astype(np.float32).mean(0) - A[neg].astype(np.float32).mean(0)


def unitL(V):  # unit-normalise each layer's vector
    return V / (np.linalg.norm(V, axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-12)


def main(which):
    D = {}
    rows, A, nll, _ = load(which, "hc3")
    ai = np.array([r["ai"] for r in rows]); tr = np.array([r["split"] == "train" for r in rows])
    dom = np.array([r["domain"] for r in rows])
    D["ai_hc3"] = dmean(A, tr & (ai == 1), tr & (ai == 0))
    hum = tr & (ai == 0)
    D["domain"] = dmean(A, hum & (dom != "reddit_eli5"), hum & (dom == "reddit_eli5"))
    wl = np.array([len(r["text"].split()) for r in rows])
    lo, hi = np.quantile(wl[hum], [1 / 3, 2 / 3])
    D["verbosity"] = dmean(A, hum & (wl >= hi), hum & (wl <= lo))
    nll_h = [(A[hum], nll[hum])]
    # projection stats on HC3 train for clamping
    rows2, A2, nll2, _ = load(which, "hap")
    gen = np.array([r["generator"] for r in rows2]); tr2 = np.array([r["split"] == "train" for r in rows2])
    dom2 = np.array([r["domain"] for r in rows2])
    isinst = np.isin(gen, list(INST_GENS))
    D["ai_hap"] = dmean(A2, tr2 & isinst, tr2 & (gen == "human"))
    h2 = tr2 & (gen == "human")
    D["register"] = dmean(A2, h2 & np.isin(dom2, ["acad", "news"]), h2 & np.isin(dom2, ["spok", "tvm", "fic"]))
    nll_h.append((A2[h2], nll2[h2]))
    Ah = np.concatenate([a for a, _ in nll_h]); nh = np.concatenate([n for _, n in nll_h])
    lo, hi = np.quantile(nh, [1 / 3, 2 / 3])
    D["fluency"] = dmean(Ah, nh <= lo, nh >= hi)
    rows3, A3, _, _ = load(which, "rewrites")
    st = np.array([r["style"] for r in rows3])
    D["formality"] = dmean(A3, st == "formal", st == "informal")
    try:
        D["assistant"] = np.load(f"{ROOT}/data/acts/{which}_assistant_axis_dir.npy")
    except FileNotFoundError:
        print("no assistant axis yet")
    U = {k: unitL(v) for k, v in D.items()}
    U["ai"] = unitL(U["ai_hc3"] + U["ai_hap"])
    # mean projections of human / AI train texts on the main direction (per layer)
    proj_h = np.concatenate([np.einsum("nld,ld->nl", A[tr & (ai == 0)].astype(np.float32), U["ai"]),
                             np.einsum("nld,ld->nl", A2[h2].astype(np.float32), U["ai"])]).mean(0)
    proj_a = np.concatenate([np.einsum("nld,ld->nl", A[tr & (ai == 1)].astype(np.float32), U["ai"]),
                             np.einsum("nld,ld->nl", A2[tr2 & isinst].astype(np.float32), U["ai"])]).mean(0)
    raw_norm = {k: np.linalg.norm(v, axis=-1) for k, v in D.items()}
    np.savez(f"{ROOT}/data/acts/{which}_directions.npz", **{f"u_{k}": v for k, v in U.items()},
             **{f"raw_{k}": v for k, v in D.items()}, proj_h=proj_h, proj_a=proj_a)
    print(which, "saved", list(U))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1])

        # Define a classifier head.
        self.classifier = nn.Linear(config.hidden_size, 1)
        # Initialize weights (handled by PreTrainedModel)
        self.init_weights()

"""Independent AI-text detectors (none of them sees Qwen activations).

supervised: three public fine-tuned classifiers, P(AI)
  desklib  : desklib/ai-text-detector-v1.01 (DeBERTa-v3-large, trained on recent LLM text)
  fakespot : fakespot-ai/roberta-base-ai-text-detection-v1
  hc3rob   : Hello-SimpleAI/chatgpt-detector-roberta (trained on HC3; reported, not used as primary)
zero-shot: Binoculars (Hans et al., 2024) with Falcon-7B (observer) / Falcon-7B-Instruct (performer).
  bino_ai = -Binoculars score (higher = more AI-like). Also returns falcon_nll (mean token NLL of
  the text under Falcon-7B), used as a model-independent fluency/coherence proxy.
"""
import os
import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoConfig, AutoModel, PreTrainedModel, AutoModelForSequenceClassification, AutoModelForCausalLM

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
os.environ.setdefault("HF_HOME", os.path.join(ROOT, "hf_cache"))


class DesklibAIDetectionModel(PreTrainedModel):
    config_class = AutoConfig

    def __init__(self, config):
        super().__init__(config)
        self.model = AutoModel.from_config(config)
        self.classifier = nn.Linear(config.hidden_size, 1)

    def forward(self, input_ids, attention_mask=None):
        h = self.model(input_ids, attention_mask=attention_mask)[0]
        m = attention_mask.unsqueeze(-1).float()
        return self.classifier((h * m).sum(1) / m.sum(1).clamp(min=1e-9))


@torch.no_grad()
def supervised_scores(texts, bs=32):
    out = {}
    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("desklib/ai-text-detector-v1.01")
    m = DesklibAIDetectionModel.from_pretrained("desklib/ai-text-detector-v1.01").cuda().eval().half()
    s = []
    for i in range(0, len(texts), bs):
        e = tok(texts[i:i + bs], padding=True, truncation=True, max_length=512, return_tensors="pt").to("cuda")
        s += torch.sigmoid(m(e.input_ids, e.attention_mask).float()).squeeze(-1).tolist()
    out["desklib"] = np.array(s); del m
    for key, name in [("fakespot", "fakespot-ai/roberta-base-ai-text-detection-v1"),
                      ("hc3rob", "Hello-SimpleAI/chatgpt-detector-roberta")]:
        tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(name)
        m = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(name).cuda().eval().half()
        s = []
        for i in range(0, len(texts), bs):
            e = tok(texts[i:i + bs], padding=True, truncation=True, max_length=512, return_tensors="pt").to("cuda")
            s += torch.softmax(m(**e).logits.float(), -1)[:, 1].tolist()
        out[key] = np.array(s); del m
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
    return out


@torch.no_grad()
def binoculars(texts, bs=8, max_len=256):
    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("tiiuae/falcon-7b")
    tok.pad_token = tok.eos_token
    obs = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("tiiuae/falcon-7b", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16).cuda().eval()
    perf = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("tiiuae/falcon-7b-instruct", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16).cuda().eval()
    B, NLL = [], []
    for i in range(0, len(texts), bs):
        e = tok([t if t.strip() else "." for t in texts[i:i + bs]], padding=True, truncation=True,
                max_length=max_len, return_tensors="pt").to("cuda")
        lo = obs(**e).logits[:, :-1].float()
        lp = perf(**e).logits[:, :-1].float()
        tgt = e.input_ids[:, 1:]
        m = e.attention_mask[:, 1:].float()
        nll = torch.nn.functional.cross_entropy(lp.transpose(1, 2), tgt, reduction="none")  # performer ppl
        nll_obs = torch.nn.functional.cross_entropy(lo.transpose(1, 2), tgt, reduction="none")
        xent = -(torch.softmax(lo, -1) * torch.log_softmax(lp, -1)).sum(-1)  # cross-perplexity
        ppl = (nll * m).sum(1) / m.sum(1).clamp(min=1)
        x = (xent * m).sum(1) / m.sum(1).clamp(min=1)
        B += (ppl / x).tolist()
        NLL += ((nll_obs * m).sum(1) / m.sum(1).clamp(min=1)).tolist()
    del obs, perf
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
    return {"bino_ai": -np.array(B), "falcon_nll": np.array(NLL)}

"""Batch chat completion with a local vLLM model (run inside .venv-vllm).
usage: python vllm_chat.py MODEL in.jsonl out.jsonl [temperature] [max_tokens]
in.jsonl rows: {"id": ..., "messages": [...]}; out rows: {"id": ..., "output": ...}"""
import json, os, sys
ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
os.environ.setdefault("HF_HOME", os.path.join(ROOT, "hf_cache"))
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

model, inp, out = sys.argv[1:4]
temp = float(sys.argv[4]) if len(sys.argv) > 4 else 0.0
mx = int(sys.argv[5]) if len(sys.argv) > 5 else 400
rows = [json.loads(l) for l in open(inp)]
llm = LLM(model=model, dtype="bfloat16", max_model_len=4096, gpu_memory_utilization=0.85, seed=0)
outs = llm.chat([r["messages"] for r in rows], SamplingParams(temperature=temp, top_p=0.95 if temp > 0 else 1.0,
                                                              max_tokens=mx, seed=0))
with open(out, "w") as f:
    for r, o in zip(rows, outs):
        f.write(json.dumps({"id": r["id"], "output": o.outputs[0].text}) + "\n")
print("wrote", len(rows))

"""Content-matched control corpora made by rewriting human text with a local LLM
(Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct via vLLM -- a different family from the Qwen model we probe).

For each human source passage:
  formal   - very formal register
  informal - very casual register
  neutral  - a plain paraphrase (content fixed, author becomes an LLM)
formal-vs-informal gives a FORMALITY direction with authorship held fixed (both AI);
human-vs-neutral gives an AUTHORSHIP contrast with content held fixed.
usage: python make_rewrites.py prep   (writes the request file)
       python make_rewrites.py collect (after vllm_chat.py has run)
"""
import json, random, sys
from common import load_jsonl, ROOT

random.seed(1)
REQ = f"{ROOT}/data/processed/rewrite_requests.jsonl"
OUT = f"{ROOT}/data/processed/rewrite_outputs.jsonl"
INSTR = {
    "formal": "Rewrite the following passage in a highly formal, academic register. Keep the same content and roughly the same length.",
    "informal": "Rewrite the following passage in a very casual, informal, conversational register (as if texting a friend). Keep the same content and roughly the same length.",
    "neutral": "Paraphrase the following passage. Keep the same content, meaning and roughly the same length.",
}


def sources():
    hap = [r for r in load_jsonl(f"{ROOT}/data/processed/hap.jsonl") if r["ai"] == 0 and r["split"] == "train"]
    hc3 = [r for r in load_jsonl(f"{ROOT}/data/processed/hc3.jsonl") if r["ai"] == 0 and r["split"] == "train"]
    return random.sample(hap, 300) + random.sample(hc3, 200)


if sys.argv[1] == "prep":
    with open(REQ, "w") as f:
        for i, r in enumerate(sources()):
            for style, ins in INSTR.items():
                msg = f"{ins} Output only the rewritten passage, with no preamble or comments.\n\nPassage:\n{' '.join(r['text'].split()[:200])}"
                f.write(json.dumps({"id": f"{i}|{style}", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": msg}]}) + "\n")
else:
    src = sources()
    outs = {r["id"]: r["output"] for r in load_jsonl(OUT)}
    rows = []
    for i, r in enumerate(src):
        rows.append(dict(text=" ".join(r["text"].split()[:200]), style="human", group=f"rw_{i}",
                         source_dataset=r["dataset"], domain=r["domain"], ai=0))
        for style in INSTR:
            o = outs[f"{i}|{style}"].strip()
            if o.lower().startswith(("here is", "here's")) and "\n" in o:
                o = o.split("\n", 1)[1].strip()
            rows.append(dict(text=o, style=style, group=f"rw_{i}", source_dataset=r["dataset"], domain=r["domain"], ai=1))
    with open(f"{ROOT}/data/processed/rewrites.jsonl", "w") as f:
        for r in rows:
            f.write(json.dumps(r) + "\n")
    print(len(rows))

"""Content-matched control corpora made by rewriting human text with an external LLM.

For each human source passage we ask Cohere Command A for
  formal   - very formal register
  informal - very casual register
  neutral  - a plain paraphrase (content fixed, author becomes an LLM)
formal-vs-informal gives a FORMALITY direction with authorship held fixed (both AI);
human-vs-neutral gives an AUTHORSHIP contrast with content held fixed.
"""
import json, random
from common import load_jsonl, ROOT
from llm_api import chat_many

random.seed(1)
MODEL = "cohere:command-a-03-2025"
hap = [r for r in load_jsonl(f"{ROOT}/data/processed/hap.jsonl") if r["ai"] == 0 and r["split"] == "train"]
hc3 = [r for r in load_jsonl(f"{ROOT}/data/processed/hc3.jsonl") if r["ai"] == 0 and r["split"] == "train"]
src = random.sample(hap, 250) + random.sample(hc3, 150)
INSTR = {
    "formal": "Rewrite the following passage in a highly formal, academic register. Keep the same content and roughly the same length.",
    "informal": "Rewrite the following passage in a very casual, informal, conversational register (as if texting a friend). Keep the same content and roughly the same length.",
    "neutral": "Paraphrase the following passage. Keep the same content, meaning and roughly the same length.",
}
rows = []
for style, ins in INSTR.items():
    msgs = [[{"role": "user", "content": f"{ins} Output only the rewritten passage, nothing else.\n\nPassage:\n{' '.join(r['text'].split()[:220])}"}] for r in src]
    outs = chat_many(MODEL, msgs, temperature=0.7, max_tokens=500)

"""Read-out analysis: does the AI direction separate human vs AI text, does it transfer
across datasets / generators, is it distinct from the confound directions, and how does
it compare between base and instruct models?
usage: python analysis_readout.py   (needs directions for both models)
Writes results/readout_*.json/csv.
"""
import json, os
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy.stats import spearmanr
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from directions import load, INST_GENS
from common import ROOT

R = f"{ROOT}/results"
os.makedirs(R, exist_ok=True)
MODELS = [m for m in ["instruct", "base"] if os.path.exists(f"{ROOT}/data/acts/{m}_directions.npz")]


def auc(s, y):
    return float(roc_auc_score(y, s))


def eval_sets(which):
    """name -> (acts [N,L,d] fp16, y, extra dict) for held-out evaluation."""
    S = {}
    rows, A, nll, ntok = load(which, "hc3")
    y = np.array([r["ai"] for r in rows]); te = np.array([r["split"] == "test" for r in rows])
    wl = np.array([len(r["text"].split()) for r in rows])
    S["HC3 (ChatGPT)"] = (A[te], y[te], dict(nll=nll[te], words=wl[te]))
    rows, A, nll, ntok = load(which, "hap")
    gen = np.array([r["generator"] for r in rows]); te = np.array([r["split"] == "test" for r in rows])
    wl = np.array([len(r["text"].split()) for r in rows])
    for g in ["gpt-4o", "gpt-4o-mini", "llama3-70b-inst", "llama3-8b-inst", "llama3-70b-base", "llama3-8b-base"]:
        m = te & np.isin(gen, ["human", g])
        S[f"HAP {g}"] = (A[m], (gen[m] != "human").astype(int), dict(nll=nll[m], words=wl[m]))
    rows, A, nll, ntok = load(which, "mage")
    gen = np.array([r["generator"] for r in rows]); y = np.array([r["ai"] for r in rows])
    chat = np.array(["gpt-3.5" in g or "davinci-003" in g for g in gen])
    wl = np.array([len(r["text"].split()) for r in rows])
    for name, m in [("MAGE chat (GPT-3.5/davinci-003)", (y == 0) | chat), ("MAGE older LMs", (y == 0) | ((y == 1) & ~chat))]:
        S[name] = (A[m], y[m], dict(nll=nll[m], words=wl[m]))
    rows, A, nll, ntok = load(which, "mage_gpt4")
    y = np.array([r["ai"] for r in rows]); wl = np.array([len(r["text"].split()) for r in rows])
    S["MAGE GPT-4 (OOD)"] = (A, y, dict(nll=nll, words=wl))
    rows, A, nll, ntok = load(which, "rewrites")
    st = np.array([r["style"] for r in rows]); m = np.isin(st, ["human", "neutral"])
    wl = np.array([len(r["text"].split()) for r in rows])
    S["Llama-3.1 paraphrase"] = (A[m], (st[m] == "neutral").astype(int), dict(nll=nll[m], words=wl[m]))
    return S


def train_xy(which, layer):
    X, Y = [], []
    rows, A, _, _ = load(which, "hc3")
    tr = np.array([r["split"] == "train" for r in rows])
    X.append(A[tr, layer]); Y.append(np.array([r["ai"] for r in rows])[tr])
    rows, A, _, _ = load(which, "hap")
    gen = np.array([r["generator"] for r in rows]); tr = np.array([r["split"] == "train" for r in rows])
    m = tr & (np.isin(gen, list(INST_GENS)) | (gen == "human"))
    X.append(A[m, layer]); Y.append((gen[m] != "human").astype(int))
    return np.concatenate(X).astype(np.float32), np.concatenate(Y)


def main():
    out = {}
    dirs = {m: np.load(f"{ROOT}/data/acts/{m}_directions.npz") for m in MODELS}
    sets = {m: eval_sets(m) for m in MODELS}
    L = dirs[MODELS[0]]["u_ai"].shape[0]
    # ---- 1. layer sweep of the diff-of-means directions -----------------------
    rec = []
    for m in MODELS:
        for name, (A, y, ex) in sets[m].items():
            for l in range(1, L):
                for dname in ["ai", "ai_hc3", "ai_hap"]:
                    s = A[:, l].astype(np.float32) @ dirs[m][f"u_{dname}"][l]
                    rec.append(dict(model=m, eval=name, layer=l, direction=dname, auroc=auc(s, y)))
    sweep = pd.DataFrame(rec); sweep.to_csv(f"{R}/readout_layer_sweep.csv", index=False)
    # pick layer: best mean AUROC of the pooled direction across held-out sets (instruct)
    piv = sweep[(sweep.model == "instruct") & (sweep.direction == "ai")].groupby("layer").auroc.mean()
    best = int(piv.idxmax()); out["best_layer_instruct_readout"] = best
    print("mean AUROC by layer (instruct)", piv.round(3).to_dict())
    LAYERS = sorted(set([best, 14, 16, 20]))
    out["layers_reported"] = LAYERS
    # ---- 2. probe vs diff-of-means and controls at reported layers -----------
    rec = []
    for m in MODELS:
        for l in LAYERS:
            Xtr, Ytr = train_xy(m, l)
            sc = StandardScaler().fit(Xtr)
            clf = LogisticRegression(C=0.01, max_iter=3000).fit(sc.transform(Xtr), Ytr)
            for name, (A, y, ex) in sets[m].items():
                X = A[:, l].astype(np.float32)
                r = dict(model=m, layer=l, eval=name, n=len(y),
                         dom_ai=auc(X @ dirs[m]["u_ai"][l], y),
                         probe=auc(clf.decision_function(sc.transform(X)), y),
                         neg_nll=auc(-ex["nll"], y), words=auc(ex["words"], y))
                for c in ["formality", "register", "domain", "fluency", "verbosity", "assistant"]:
                    if f"u_{c}" in dirs[m].files:
                        r[f"dir_{c}"] = auc(X @ dirs[m][f"u_{c}"][l], y)
                rec.append(r)
    tab = pd.DataFrame(rec); tab.to_csv(f"{R}/readout_auroc.csv", index=False)
    # ---- 3. geometry: cosines with confound directions ------------------------
    rec = []
    for m in MODELS:
        d = dirs[m]
        names = [k[2:] for k in d.files if k.startswith("u_")]
        for l in range(1, L):
            for a in names:
                for b in names:
                    if a < b:
                        rec.append(dict(model=m, layer=l, a=a, b=b, cos=float(d[f"u_{a}"][l] @ d[f"u_{b}"][l])))
    cos = pd.DataFrame(rec); cos.to_csv(f"{R}/readout_cosines.csv", index=False)
    # ---- 4. nullspace test: remove confound subspace, refit, re-evaluate -------
    rec = []
    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
    for m in MODELS:
        d = dirs[m]
        conf = [c for c in ["formality", "register", "domain", "fluency", "verbosity", "assistant"] if f"u_{c}" in d.files]
        for l in LAYERS:
            Xtr, Ytr = train_xy(m, l)
            C = np.stack([d[f"raw_{c}"][l] for c in conf]).astype(np.float64)
            Q, _ = np.linalg.qr(C.T)  # d x k orthonormal basis of confound span
            Qr, _ = np.linalg.qr(rng.standard_normal(Q.shape))
            Qai = d["u_ai"][l][:, None]
            u0 = d["u_ai"][l]
            frac = float(np.sum((Q.T @ u0) ** 2))
            for tag, B in [("none", None), ("confounds", Q), ("random_k", Qr), ("ai_dir", Qai)]:
                P = (lambda X: X) if B is None else (lambda X, B=B: X - (X @ B) @ B.T)
                Xp = P(Xtr.astype(np.float64))
                u = Xp[Ytr == 1].mean(0) - Xp[Ytr == 0].mean(0)
                for name, (A, y, ex) in sets[m].items():
                    rec.append(dict(model=m, layer=l, removed=tag, k=0 if B is None else B.shape[1], eval=name,
                                    auroc=auc(P(A[:, l].astype(np.float64)) @ u, y), frac_ai_in_conf_span=frac))
    ns = pd.DataFrame(rec); ns.to_csv(f"{R}/readout_nullspace.csv", index=False)
    # ---- 5. scalar confounds: NLL / length partial out ------------------------
    rec = []
    for m in MODELS:
        l = best
        for name, (A, y, ex) in sets[m].items():
            s = A[:, l].astype(np.float32) @ dirs[m]["u_ai"][l]
            Z = np.stack([ex["nll"], np.log(ex["words"] + 1)], 1)
            base = LogisticRegression(max_iter=2000).fit(Z, y)
            full = LogisticRegression(max_iter=2000).fit(np.c_[Z, s], y)
            r = dict(model=m, layer=l, eval=name,
                     auroc_nll_len=auc(base.decision_function(Z), y),
                     auroc_nll_len_plus_dir=auc(full.decision_function(np.c_[Z, s]), y),
                     rho_dir_nll_human=float(spearmanr(s[y == 0], ex["nll"][y == 0])[0]),
                     rho_dir_nll_ai=float(spearmanr(s[y == 1], ex["nll"][y == 1])[0]),
                     rho_dir_len_human=float(spearmanr(s[y == 0], ex["words"][y == 0])[0]),
                     rho_dir_len_ai=float(spearmanr(s[y == 1], ex["words"][y == 1])[0]))
            # direction AUROC after residualising the score on NLL & length (linear)
            beta = np.linalg.lstsq(np.c_[np.ones(len(s)), Z], s, rcond=None)[0]
            r["auroc_dir_resid"] = auc(s - np.c_[np.ones(len(s)), Z] @ beta, y)
            rec.append(r)
    pd.DataFrame(rec).to_csv(f"{R}/readout_scalar_confounds.csv", index=False)
    # ---- 6. base vs instruct ---------------------------------------------------
    if len(MODELS) == 2:
        rec = []
        di, db = dirs["instruct"], dirs["base"]
        for l in range(1, L):
            r = dict(layer=l, cos_ai_base_inst=float(di["u_ai"][l] @ db["u_ai"][l]),
                     cos_formality_base_inst=float(di["u_formality"][l] @ db["u_formality"][l]))
            if "u_assistant" in di.files and "u_assistant" in db.files:
                r["cos_assistant_base_inst"] = float(di["u_assistant"][l] @ db["u_assistant"][l])
            for name in sets["instruct"]:
                Ai, y, _ = sets["instruct"][name]; Ab, yb, _ = sets["base"][name]
                si = Ai[:, l].astype(np.float32) @ di["u_ai"][l]
                sb = Ab[:, l].astype(np.float32) @ db["u_ai"][l]
                sx = Ai[:, l].astype(np.float32) @ db["u_ai"][l]  # base direction read in instruct model
                dprime = lambda s, y: float((s[y == 1].mean() - s[y == 0].mean()) / np.sqrt(0.5 * (s[y == 1].var() + s[y == 0].var())))
                r[f"{name}|inst_auc"] = auc(si, y); r[f"{name}|base_auc"] = auc(sb, yb); r[f"{name}|base_dir_on_inst_auc"] = auc(sx, y)
                r[f"{name}|inst_d"] = dprime(si, y); r[f"{name}|base_d"] = dprime(sb, yb)
            rec.append(r)
        pd.DataFrame(rec).to_csv(f"{R}/readout_base_vs_instruct.csv", index=False)
    json.dump(out, open(f"{R}/readout_summary.json", "w"), indent=1)
    print(out)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""LLM-judge (Gemma-3-12B-it, local via vLLM; a different model family from Qwen,
the detectors and the rewriter).
usage: python judge.py prep  in.jsonl req.jsonl     (rows need id, question, text)
       python judge.py parse req_out.jsonl parsed.jsonl
"""
import json, re, sys

PROMPT = """You are an expert at distinguishing human-written text from text written by AI chatbots (like ChatGPT, Claude, Llama or Qwen).

Below is a question and a response to it. Rate the RESPONSE on three 1-10 scales:
- ai_likeness: how likely the response was written by an AI chatbot rather than a human (for example a person answering on a forum or Q&A site). 1 = certainly human, 10 = certainly AI.
- coherence: is it fluent, grammatical, well-formed and logically coherent text? 1 = gibberish or broken/repetitive, 10 = perfectly coherent.
- relevance: does it actually address the question? 1 = unrelated, 10 = directly and fully on topic.

Question: {q}

Response:
\"\"\"
{t}
\"\"\"

Answer with only a JSON object of the form {{"ai_likeness": <int>, "coherence": <int>, "relevance": <int>}}."""


def prep(inp, out):
    with open(out, "w") as f:
        for l in open(inp):
            r = json.loads(l)
            t = " ".join(r["text"].split()[:300]) or "(empty)"
            f.write(json.dumps({"id": r["id"], "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": PROMPT.format(q=r["question"], t=t)}]}) + "\n")


def parse(inp, out):
    bad = 0
    with open(out, "w") as f:
        for l in open(inp):
            r = json.loads(l)
            d = {}
            for k in ["ai_likeness", "coherence", "relevance"]:
                m = re.search(rf'"{k}"\s*:\s*(\d+)', r["output"])
                d[k] = int(m.group(1)) if m else None
            bad += any(v is None for v in d.values())
            f.write(json.dumps({"id": r["id"], **d}) + "\n")
    print("unparsed", bad)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    {"prep": prep, "parse": parse}[sys.argv[1]](*sys.argv[2:])

"""Generate steered outputs.
usage:
  python run_steering.py pilot                 # layer x strength pilot on 40 prompts (instruct)
  python run_steering.py main LAYER            # full condition grid on 160 held-out HC3 questions (instruct)
  python run_steering.py base LAYER            # base model: continuation of human text prefixes
Outputs results/steering/{name}.jsonl (id, cond, family, alpha, layer, question, text).
Strength a is in units of the human-AI gap along the AI direction at that layer (a=-1 moves
the residual stream by exactly the human-AI mean difference towards human); every control
vector gets the same absolute L2 norm.
"""
import json, os, sys, time
import numpy as np
import torch
from common import load_model, load_jsonl, ROOT
from steer import Steerer, generate, random_unit

OUT = f"{ROOT}/results/steering"
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
HUMAN_SYS = ("Answer the way an ordinary person would when replying on an online forum such as Reddit. "
             "Write casually and naturally, like a human, and do not sound like an AI assistant.")


def run(name, which, prompts, conds, chat=True, max_new_tokens=200):
    path = f"{OUT}/{name}.jsonl"
    done = set()
    if os.path.exists(path):
        done = {json.loads(l)["cond"] for l in open(path)}
    tok, model = load_model(which)
    D = np.load(f"{ROOT}/data/acts/{which}_directions.npz")
    st = Steerer(model)
    with open(path, "a") as f:
        for c in conds:
            if c["cond"] in done:
                continue
            t = time.time()
            st.clear()
            if c["kind"] == "add":
                l = c["layer"]
                gap = float(D["proj_a"][l] - D["proj_h"][l])
                v = c["vec"](D, l, model.config.hidden_size)
                st.add(l, c["alpha"] * gap * v)
            elif c["kind"] == "clamp":
                for l in c["layers"]:
                    st.clamp(l, D["u_ai"][l], float(D[c["target"]][l]))
            outs = generate(tok, model, [p["question"] for p in prompts], system=c.get("system"),
                            max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens, chat=chat)
            st.clear()
            for p, o in zip(prompts, outs):
                f.write(json.dumps(dict(id=p["id"], cond=c["cond"], family=c["family"], alpha=c.get("alpha", 0.0),
                                        layer=c.get("layer"), question=p["question"], text=o)) + "\n")
            f.flush()
            print(name, c["cond"], f"{time.time()-t:.0f}s", "|", outs[0][:150].replace("\n", " "), flush=True)
    del model; torch.cuda.empty_cache()


U = lambda key: (lambda D, l, d: D[key][l])
RAND = lambda seed: (lambda D, l, d: random_unit(d, 1000 * seed + l))


def add(family, vec, alpha, layer, **kw):
    return dict(cond=f"{family}@L{layer}a{alpha:+g}", family=family, kind="add", vec=vec, alpha=alpha, layer=layer, **kw)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    mode = sys.argv[1]
    P = load_jsonl(f"{ROOT}/data/processed/steer_prompts.jsonl")
    if mode == "pilot":
        prompts = [p for i, p in enumerate(P) if i % 4 == 0]  # 40 prompts, all domains
        conds = [dict(cond="none", family="none", kind="none")]
        for l in [8, 12, 16, 20]:
            for a in [-8, -4, -2, 2, 4, 8]:
                conds.append(add("ai", U("u_ai"), a, l))
        run("pilot", "instruct", prompts, conds)
    elif mode == "main":
        L = int(sys.argv[2]); A = [float(x) for x in sys.argv[3].split(",")]
        conds = [dict(cond="none", family="none", kind="none"),
                 dict(cond="prompt_human", family="prompt_human", kind="none", system=HUMAN_SYS)]
        for a in A:
            conds.append(add("ai", U("u_ai"), a, L))
        for a in A:
            conds.append(add("ai", U("u_ai"), a, L, system=HUMAN_SYS) | dict(cond=f"ai+prompt@L{L}a{a:+g}", family="ai+prompt_human")) if a < 0 else None
        conds = [c for c in conds if c]
        for a in A:
            for s in range(3):
                conds.append(add(f"random{s}", RAND(s), a, L))
            for fam in ["formality", "assistant", "fluency", "register"]:
                conds.append(add(fam, U(f"u_{fam}"), a, L))
        nl = 28
        conds.append(dict(cond="clamp_human", family="clamp_human", kind="clamp", layers=list(range(1, nl)), target="proj_h"))
        conds.append(dict(cond="clamp_ai", family="clamp_ai", kind="clamp", layers=list(range(1, nl)), target="proj_a"))
        run("main", "instruct", P, conds)
    elif mode == "base":
        L = int(sys.argv[2]); A = [float(x) for x in sys.argv[3].split(",")]
        hap = [r for r in load_jsonl(f"{ROOT}/data/processed/hap.jsonl") if r["generator"] == "human" and r["split"] == "test"]

        c1 = pd.read_parquet(f"{ROOT}/data/human-ai-parallel-corpus/text_data/hape-text_human-chunk-1.parquet")

    tok, model = load_model(which)
    D = np.load(f"{ROOT}/data/acts/{which}_directions.npz")
    st = Steerer(model)
    with open(path, "a") as f:
        for c in conds:
            if c["cond"] in done:
                continue
            t = time.time()
            st.clear()
            if c["kind"] == "add":
                l = c["layer"]
                gap = float(D["proj_a"][l] - D["proj_h"][l])
                v = c["vec"](D, l, model.config.hidden_size)
                st.add(l, c["alpha"] * gap * v)

            outs = generate(tok, model, [p["question"] for p in prompts], system=c.get("system"),
                            max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens, chat=chat)
            st.clear()

                f.write(json.dumps(dict(id=p["id"], cond=c["cond"], family=c["family"], alpha=c.get("alpha", 0.0),

content.thinking: The diff-of-means direction performs well (AUROC ~0.98 at L27, probe ~1.0) but fails on base-model and older LM text, and even after removing the confound span it still holds up. I'll build a confound-orthogonalized version of the direction for steering.

input.command:
cd /workspaces/is-there-a-sounds-like-ai-direction-c164-zeroshot-claude-opus-5-5/src; python - <<'EOF'
s=open('directions.py').read()
s=s.replace('''    U["ai"] = unitL(U["ai_hc3"] + U["ai_hap"])
''','''    U["ai"] = unitL(U["ai_hc3"] + U["ai_hap"])
    # confound-orthogonal AI direction: u_ai with the span of all confound directions removed
    conf = [c for c in ["formality", "register", "domain", "fluency", "verbosity", "assistant"] if c in D]
    perp = np.zeros_like(U["ai"])
    for l in range(U["ai"].shape[0]):
        Q, _ = np.linalg.qr(np.stack([D[c][l] for c in conf]).T.astype(np.float64))
        perp[l] = U["ai"][l] - Q @ (Q.T @ U["ai"][l])
    U["ai_perp"] = unitL(perp)
''')
s=s.replace('''proj_h=proj_h, proj_a=proj_a)''','''proj_h=proj_h, proj_a=proj_a, proj_h_perp=ph2, proj_a_perp=pa2)''')
s=s.replace('''    raw_norm = {''','''    ph2 = np.concatenate([np.einsum("nld,ld->nl", A[tr & (ai == 0)].astype(np.float32), U["ai_perp"]),
                          np.einsum("nld,ld->nl", A2[h2].astype(np.float32), U["ai_perp"])]).mean(0)
    pa2 = np.concatenate([np.einsum("nld,ld->nl", A[tr & (ai == 1)].astype(np.float32), U["ai_perp"]),
                          np.einsum("nld,ld->nl", A2[tr2 & isinst].astype(np.float32), U["ai_perp"])]).mean(0)
    raw_norm = {''')
s=s.replace('''  ai       : unit(unit(ai_hc3) + unit(ai_hap))  <- main "AI-ness" direction''','''  ai       : unit(unit(ai_hc3) + unit(ai_hap))  <- main "AI-ness" direction
  ai_perp  : ai with the span of the six confound directions projected out''')
open('directions.py','w').write(s)
EOF

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: simplify

commands.name: batch

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts

commands.name: doctor

Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: azure-gpu
commands.description: Request, use and release Azure GPU VMs (A100/H100/T4) for training, RL fine-tuning, vLLM serving or paper-replication jobs. Use whenever a task needs a GPU and none is attached to this machine. Wraps `az` with size allowlist, TTL tags, auto-shutdown and a reaper so nothing is left running. (user)

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: docx
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: google-workspace
commands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files. (claude.ai sync)

If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pptx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: xlsx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved. (claude.ai sync)
